Key Responsibilities

Desirable

JOB TITLE: Cost Engineer

Location: Warrington or Preston, UK (on site 3 days per week)

Sector: Water Infrastructure

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience. 40-hour week.

Help deliver a once-in-a-generation investment in the UK's water infrastructure.

PACE Global is recruiting Cost Engineers on behalf of our client to support a major water utility's capital investment programme, working within the delivery team of a leading global engineering consultancy.

The AMP8 investment cycle (2025-2030) represents a multi-billion-pound commitment to upgrading water and wastewater networks, treatment works and environmental performance across the region.

The Opportunity

These are practitioner-level (mid-range) positions, though strong senior candidates will also be considered. You will sit within the consultancy's delivery team, working alongside project managers, planners, commercial and risk professionals, and will be accountable for the cost control, forecasting and reporting of a portfolio of water infrastructure schemes. Roles are based on site in either Warrington or Preston three days per week, on a 40-hour working week.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting into the cost management lead, your core duties will include:

  • Delivering end-to-end cost management across a portfolio of water and wastewater capital schemes, from early development through to delivery and close-out

  • Establishing and maintaining budgets, cost baselines and cost breakdown structures aligned to the programme's controls framework

  • Producing monthly cost reports covering actuals, accruals, commitments and forecasts (EAC/ETC), with clear commentary for client and delivery-partner stakeholders

  • Carrying out variance analysis against budget and forecast, identifying drivers and recommending corrective actions

  • Applying earned value management and other performance-measurement techniques to track project health

  • Supporting change control by assessing the cost impact of scope changes, trends, early warnings and risks

  • Working closely with planners, quantity surveyors, risk managers and project managers to integrate cost with schedule and risk

  • Presenting cost positions and insights to client and delivery-partner stakeholders with confidence and clarity

About You

We're looking for established cost professionals who can hit the ground running in a fast-moving, multi-stakeholder programme environment.

You'll ideally have:

  • Solid practitioner-level experience in cost management / cost engineering on major capital projects (senior-level candidates also welcomed)

  • A degree (or equivalent) in quantity surveying, engineering, construction or a related discipline, or comparable experience

  • Strong Excel skills and proficiency with cost management systems (e.g. Prism, EcoSys, SAP, Oracle Unifier or similar)

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, comfortable presenting to client and delivery-partner teams

  • The right to work in the UK and the ability to be on site in Warrington or Preston three days per week

  • Background within sectors such as Water, Utilities, Infrastructure, Energy or Construction

Desirable

  • Working knowledge of NEC contracts (NEC3/NEC4) and earned value methodologies

  • Previous experience on regulated water frameworks or earlier AMP cycles (AMP6/AMP7)

Why Join?

  • Work on one of the most significant water infrastructure investment programmes in UK history

  • A long-term pipeline of work through to 2030, with genuine scope for career progression

  • Hybrid working pattern: three days on site in Warrington or Preston, the rest remote

Apply

job.title: IMS Auditor
job.description:
Job Title: Integrated Management System (IMS) Auditor

Location: Based in our London office with hybrid working available

Vacancy Overview:

Are you looking for a career which is rewarding, at the cutting edge of project development and where you can really make a difference? Come and join our expanding Sizewell C (SZC) team and work on one of the most exciting and largest megaprojects in the UK, whilst being at the forefront of the UK’s climate change agenda and energy policy. The project has started construction and is now seeking private investment. When completed, it will provide dependable electricity to 6 million homes for 60 years, which along with renewables, will support Britain to achieve Net Zero by 2050.

Job Purpose / Overview:

The IMS Auditor provides independent, objective and evidence-based assurance on the adequacy, implementation and effectiveness. The role plans and delivers risk-based IMS audits, targeted and functional IMS audit activities, produces clear and well-written reports, verifies action close-out, and supports continual improvement across a fast-paced, highly regulated project environment.

Principal Accountabilities:

• Develop, maintain and deliver a risk-based IMS audit and functional Annual Audit programme aligned to project priorities, certification requirements and regulatory expectations.

• Plan and conduct IMS audits, targeted interventions using interviews, document review, sampling, observation and testing of objective evidence.

• Assess whether IMS arrangements are not only documented, but are understood, implemented, controlled and effective in practice across the client organisation and key interfaces.

• Produce concise, factual and well-structured reports that clearly set out scope, evidence, findings, conclusions, risks, good practice and improvement opportunities.

• Embedding and strengthening Root Cause Analysis (RCA) initiatives by ensuring all actions from audits and oversight activities are tracked through to closure, with corrective actions verified as timely, proportionate, and demonstrably effective

• Identify recurring weaknesses, emerging themes and systemic issues, and provide meaningful management information and trend analysis to support decision-making and organisational learning. • Build strong and credible working relationships across all levels of the organisation while maintaining auditor independence and the confidence to challenge difficult auditees constructively.

• Support external audits, certification activity, and assurance reviews as required, and contribute to continual improvement of the Integrated Management System including supporting development of Annual Audit Programme.

Knowledge, Skills, Qualifications, Experience:

• Strong IMS audit, assurance or oversight capability within a regulated environment.

• Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex evidence into clear, balanced and defensible reports.

• Strong interviewing, questioning and listening skills, with the confidence to probe below the surface and test assumptions.

• Ability to analyse trends, assess significance and make evidence-based judgements.

• Good understanding of integrated management systems and standards including ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 and ISO 19443.

• Good working knowledge of ISO 19011 principles and modern audit practice.

• Credible stakeholder engagement skills, able to influence constructively without losing independence.

• Strong organisation, prioritisation and follow-through in a fast-paced changing environment.

Desirable:

• Working knowledge of nuclear governance, nuclear safety culture and major project assurance expectations.

• Experience of management of change, non-conformance, action tracking or organisational learning processes.

• Experience of using assurance data, dashboards or trend reporting to support management decision-making.

• Awareness of IAEA, ONR, Environment Agency or equivalent regulatory frameworks.

• Experience of working across complex interfaces with contractors, suppliers and delivery partners.

Qualifications & Experience:

Essential:

• Degree qualified in engineering, science, quality, business management or another relevant discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

• Recognised Lead Auditor qualification in ISO 9001 or another relevant management system discipline.

• Experience of planning and delivering risk-based audits or assurance reviews.

• Experience of working within the UK regulatory environment or an equivalent highly regulated setting.

Desirable:

• Lead Auditor qualifications in ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 27001 or ISO 19443.

• Experience within the nuclear sector or another high-hazard industry.

• Experience supporting certification, surveillance or external assurance activity.

• Experience of working with regulators, certification bodies or equivalent external stakeholders.

• Experience within large-scale infrastructure, construction or programme delivery environments.

Interested? Please send your CV to: lia.welch@paceglobal.org

job.title: Project Controls Manager
job.description:
Project Controls Manager

London- Hybrid

Responsibilities

In this crucial position, you'll hold the following key responsibilities and accountabilities:

Implement and uphold robust governance: You'll establish and maintain specific Project Controls (PC) governance, processes, and procedures across the entire project, ensuring full compliance with the relevant customer contract where applicable.

Define and control the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB): You'll be responsible for setting the project's baseline in terms of scope, cost, and schedule, and then continuously managing the governance control of these elements.

Lead scheduling teams: You'll manage scheduling staff to develop, oversee, revise, and analyse integrated project schedules. This includes all phases of project execution, along with contributions from contract partnerships and relevant sub-suppliers.

Oversee project control provisions: You'll undertake, or manage project controls staff to provide, essential cost management, change management, risk and opportunity management, and document management.

Deliver comprehensive reporting: You'll provide regular management reporting, both internal and external to the project. This will ensure relevant, accurate, and reliable information on the project's status and forecast, enabling project and programme managers to make informed decisions and present an accurate view of the project's standing.

Interrogate subcontractor data: You'll scrutinise subcontractor data related to project controls to inform the project PMB and monitor their delivery performance.

Validate project success: You'll gather independent evidence to provide confidence that the project is likely to achieve its success criteria.

Integrate project control toolsets: You'll ensure the integration and alignment of project control toolsets, including across contract partnerships and relevant sub-suppliers where necessary.

Deputise for the Project Manager: You'll step in for the Project Manager as required, ensuring continuity.

Establish and analyse Earned Value Management (EVM): You'll set up a reliable and accurate Earned Value Management (EVM) system, then continuously generate and interrogate earned value reports. This will ensure reporting is completed in accordance with the contract and enable project and/or programme managers to make informed decisions.

Implement ongoing risk management: You'll establish and manage a continuous and regular risk management process throughout the team, including risk reporting and schedule risk analysis in line with the contract.

Support Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBR): You'll support Integrated Baseline Reviews (potentially with customer stakeholders) as needed to build confidence in the Performance Measurement Baseline.

Mentor and develop staff: You'll develop and mentor staff to ensure robust succession planning is in place.

Maintain key project documentation: You'll ensure all key project control documentation is meticulously maintained and updated as necessary.

Ensure effective configuration control: You'll guarantee that effective configuration control is consistently maintained at all times.

Provide progress and metrics reports: You'll furnish weekly and monthly Project Progress and Metrics Reports as appropriate for the project.

Experience

We're looking for an organised, confident communicator who is also self-motivated and possesses the knack for transforming complex problems into simple, elegant solutions. You'll need to be capable of working across a portfolio of projects and business initiatives, often at short notice.

You'll need proven experience in a similar role, demonstrating the ability to lead from the front. Additionally, you'll require strong communication and influencing skills as you'll work closely with many internal and external stakeholders.

We would also like you to have experience in a number of the following areas:

Extensive experience in project controls on complex or major projects/programmes.

Comprehensive knowledge of project controls approaches and practices, such as planning/scheduling management, cost management, risk management and analysis, performance management (i.e., EVM), change management, and configuration control.

Practical experience working with common project controls toolsets, such as MSP / P6, RiskHive, ERP / SAP systems etc.

A clear focus on project outcomes and an ability to encourage others to strive for the greater good.

Experience collaborating with multi-disciplinary teams, including external suppliers and customers.
